methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $12M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Salient Motion is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $12M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 peers: 1 public company and 8 private entities in robotics and adjacent automation sectors, including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $12M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $24M. Peer-median analysis examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B), producing a median valuation of $1.7B. The wide range reflects heterogeneity in funding stage and company maturity within the peer set.

The triangulated analysis produces a valuation range of $20M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $862M across the two methods. This wide band reflects material tension between the stage-progression approach—anchored conservatively to capital raised—and peer comparables that span Seed through Series B. Key uncertainties include the relevance of later-stage peer valuations to a Series A company and whether Salient Motion's technology, traction, or market position justify positioning near the upper quartile of the peer distribution. A narrower range would require additional data on revenue, customer concentration, or technical differentiation.
